project: Ione independent UE5 game NPC Agent prototype

claims.source_fact: Fresh author-written 10-case offline comparison: complete task success 8/10 old vs 10/10 tiered, wall-clock P50 17.21 s vs 0.62 s; 5 optimized cases used a zero-model policy path.
claims.candidate_wording: On a fresh, author-written 10-case offline set, complete task success improved 8/10 to 10/10 and wall-clock P50 fell from 17.21 s to 0.62 s.
claims.interview_details: Explain reset-world cases, fixed success rubric, tiered intent routing, tool-authored replies and the five zero-model cases.
claims.boundary: Offline prototype metric; no model capability or online player-experience claim.
risk_notes: Small author-written set; measured on one machine.

claims.source_fact: UE 5.8.4 C++ build succeeded; real game viewport showed archive scene and dialogue-driven warning and speaking full-body 2D poses.
claims.candidate_wording: Integrated a playable Unreal Engine 5.8 C++/UMG scene with free-text Agent dialogue and four authored 2D full-body poses.
claims.interview_details: Explain UMG input commit, loopback HTTP response, validated tool traces, pose assets, motion accent and engine render capture.
claims.boundary: 2D pose switching and motion accent, not a 3D rig, lip sync or continuous character animation; implementation was AI-assisted.
risk_notes: Blueprint event is emitted for verified tool success, but no visible door animation is bound.

claims.source_fact: Five bridge smoke requests passed for route, route paraphrase, record, denied door and negated door, with raw traces and unchanged locked door state.
claims.candidate_wording: A separate 5/5 live bridge smoke check validated grounded route/record answers, consent denial and no-action negation.
claims.interview_details: Show the saved tool traces and world snapshots; distinguish Python service timing from UE end-to-end latency.
claims.boundary: Bridge smoke is not a second benchmark or a human study.
risk_notes: All five checked prompts took a deterministic policy path; no LLM latency claim from this check.

claims.source_fact: The project study cites Rao et al. 2024 on Minecraft NPC collaboration and language-only game-state limits, and Chen et al. 2025 on tiered gaming Q&A.
claims.candidate_wording: After our conversation, I explored game NPC research and used the game-state grounding and tiered Q&A questions to frame an independent UE5 prototype.
claims.interview_details: User should personally review the two papers and be able to explain what each paper did versus what Ione implemented.
claims.boundary: Do not claim reproduction of either paper's full system or results.
risk_notes: Personal reading and motivation chronology must be confirmed by the user before external use.
